# Vanapattha Sutta (MN 17 (PTS MN i 104))
**ID:** MN 17 (PTS MN i 104)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Vanapattha Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vanapattha Sutta* ("Jungle Thickets", MN 17; PTS MN i 104–107) is the seventeenth discourse of the *Majjhima Nikāya*, delivered by the Buddha while staying at Sāvatthi in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Kuan 2008]. The sutta lays out the conditions under which a meditating monk should continue living in a forest dwelling or jungle thicket, and when he ought to depart [Humphreys 1956; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The Buddha teaches that a practitioner's decision to stay in a given place—or under a particular teacher—must be evaluated primarily by whether one's unestablished mindfulness becomes established, uncollected mind becomes concentrated, and unabandoned defilements are abandoned [Kuan 2008; Rogell 2003]. If spiritual progress is lacking, one should leave whether basic requisites are scarce or plentiful; if one is making spiritual progress, one should remain regardless of material conditions [Schmithausen 1991; Rogell 2003]. In early Buddhist asceticism, taming oneself through moral discipline and mental concentration is presented as essential to abiding peacefully in the wilderness without succumbing to fear [Galasek 2016]. Linguistically, the discourse is notable as a rare instance where mindfulness (*sati*) is directly coupled with the verb *upaṭṭhāti* ("stands near" or "is present") [Kuan 2008]. Regarding its composition, Govind Chandra Pande observes that although the internal text title is announced as *vanapatthapariyāya*, sections discussing settlements (*gāma*) and teachers suggest later structural extension [Pande 1974].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.6, a Sanskrit fragment from the Turfan collection (SHT sutta 73), and two Chinese Āgama parallels: Madhyama-āgama discourses MĀ 107 and MĀ 108, along with Ekottarikāgama discourse EĀ 45.3 [SuttaCentral]. It also shares themes with the *Sevitabbāsevitabba Sutta* (MN 114) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus aligns the sutta's recurring formulas with substantial internal Pali parallels, prominently in AN 5, AN 9, AN 11, and MN 52, as well as commentary in the *Papañcasūdanī* and *Visuddhimagga*; its cross-language alignments confirm close correspondences with the *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26) and Sanskrit Avadāna literature [DharmaNexus].
